messages.content: help me understand this sentence: the chair had been fixed before my aunt came to visit.
it says the chair was fixed first, and your aunt came later. the sentence does not say who fixed it unless more information is given.
can i say my aunt fixed it?
not from that sentence alone. your aunt is the person who came to visit. being in the sentence does not make her the person who did the work on the chair.
my brother did the work. put him in the sentence.
my brother had fixed the chair before my aunt came to visit.
now make the chair the first thing in the sentence again.
the chair had been fixed by my brother before my aunt came to visit.
what is different about the two sentences?
one starts with your brother and says what he did. the other starts with the chair and says what happened to it. both give your brother as the person who fixed it before the visit.
what if he was still working when she came?
then say: my brother was fixing the chair when my aunt came to visit. that puts the work and her coming together in time, rather than saying the work was already finished.
can you write a short story using that last sentence?

my brother was fixing the chair when my aunt came to visit. she stood near the garden door and asked if he needed help. he asked her to hold one part while he worked. after the chair was ready, they sat outside and talked.
i have six pieces of fruit for three children. i want each child to have the same number. how many should each get?
each child can get two pieces. two for each of three children will take all six pieces.
one child says they only want one piece now. do i have to give the other piece away?
no. you can keep it for later or ask what the children would like to do. the first plan was for the same number, but the child has given you a different choice about what they want now.
if i give one to that child and two to each other child, how many are left?
you give out five pieces: one, two, and two. one piece is left from the six.
write a sentence that makes clear the one left is not a new piece.
one of the original six pieces is still left after you give out the other five.
can i say all the children had two?
not in this new plan. two children had two pieces each, and one child had one. you changed the first plan after hearing what that child wanted.
what question can i ask about the last piece?
would anyone like the last piece now, or should we keep it for later?
if nobody wants it now, does that mean nobody likes fruit?
no. they may have had enough for now or want it later. one answer about this piece at this time does not tell you what everyone likes in general.
my aunt sent me a voice message today. she was talking about something simple, but hearing her voice made me think of being at her house when i was little.
a voice you know well can bring a place or time to mind. what did you remember about being there?
i remembered sitting at the kitchen table while she cooked. she would talk to me while moving around the room.
so the message brought back more than the words she was saying today. you remembered the way she talked while you sat in her kitchen.
yes. i want to tell her that without making it sound sad. it felt good.
you could say: hearing your voice today made me think of sitting in your kitchen when i was little. i liked those visits, and it was good to remember them.
i did not say every visit was good. keep it about sitting in the kitchen.
hearing your voice today made me think of sitting in your kitchen while you cooked. it felt good to remember that.
can i ask if she can remember it too?
yes. you could add: do you remember talking with me while you cooked? she may remember a different detail that you can talk about together.
what if she does not remember that part?
then your memory can still be real for you. people may remember different parts of the same time. you can tell her what you remember without asking her to give the same answer.
i spent the whole day inside and finally went for a short walk. i did not go far, but i feel better.
sometimes a small change of place is enough to make a day feel different. what did you enjoy about the walk?
i liked the air and seeing the sky. i had been looking at a screen for hours.
then the walk gave you something different to look at and time to move. it did not have to be a long journey to feel like a change.
i want to do it again tomorrow, but i do not want to make a big plan that i stop after one day.
you could keep it small: after work, i will see whether i want a short walk. that gives you a place to start without choosing a long walk every day.
i want to choose a time. i think right after work will be easiest.
then you can plan a short walk right after work. choose only a little time to start, so it feels possible, and see how it goes tomorrow.
say the plan in a simple way.
plan a short walk right after work, with only a little time needed. you can choose whether you want more once you are outside.
write a note to myself in one sentence.
after work tomorrow, i will go outside for a short walk and see how i feel.
i wrote a letter saying thank you to my teacher for helping me read. i do not know how to end it. i do not want to ask for anything else.
you can end with a simple thank you that says what the help did for you. for example: thank you for taking the time to help me. i understand more now, and i want to keep reading.
make it shorter.
you can end by saying what changed for you: thank you for helping me read. i understand more now and want to keep learning.
i want to say she waited when i read slowly. that was important to me.
thank you for waiting while i read slowly. having time to try helped me understand more, and i want to keep reading.
can i say that without asking her to do the same for every person from now on?
yes. your sentence thanks her for what she did with you. it does not by itself ask her to do anything new for anyone else.
make a short end that keeps waiting and reading.
thank you for waiting while i learned. your help made me want to keep reading.
i am still learning, so learned feels too finished.
thank you for waiting while i learn. your help makes me want to keep reading.
what changed between those two examples?
the last one has learn and makes to keep the idea about what is happening now. the other looked back at learning and help from before.
write a short story about a worker leaving a note for the person who comes next. the note should help with one small thing, not explain the whole task.

a worker was closing the shop when she saw that one shelf was still empty. the things for it were in a container under the desk. she could not finish before leaving, so she wrote a note for the next worker: the things for the empty shelf are under the desk. i have not put them out yet. in the morning, the next worker read the note, found the container, and knew where to start.
why did she say she had not put them out yet?
it made clear what was still left to do. knowing where the container was would help, but the note also needed to say the things were not yet on the shelf.
explain it another way.
she said the things were still under the desk, so the next worker would know they had not yet been put on the shelf.
does the note make every task at the shop known?
no. it helps with one shelf and one container. the next worker may still need other information for other parts of the day.
write the next worker saying thank you after doing that part.
thank you for the note. i found the container and put the things on the shelf this morning.
now write the first worker answering without adding another task.
thank you for doing that. i am happy the note helped you find it.
my child asked why i like the park. i said i like the trees. she said she likes the play area, so we cannot both like the same park. how can i explain?
you can like the same place for different reasons. you can like the trees while she enjoys the play area. your reasons do not have to be the same for the place to be good for both of you.
make an example with a room at home.

one person likes a room because it has a quiet place to read. another likes the same room because the family sits there together in the evening. both can like the room, even though they first think of different things.
she says quiet reading and family talking cannot happen at the same moment.
that is a good detail to think about. the room can be used for different things at one time and then another. if you like reading there, that does not mean it must be quiet every moment of the day.
keep that simple.
the room can be quiet for reading at one time and have people talking at another. both people can like it for what they do there.
what question could i ask my child about the park?
what do you like doing at the park, and what do you think i like doing there?
i want the question to ask for her own answer, not test if she knows mine.
then ask about her first: what do you like best about going to the park? after she answers, you can tell her what you enjoy without making it a test.
picoboi, answer my next question with one short sentence. how can i ask a friend whether they are free after work?
are you free after work today?
good. now make it about tomorrow and keep it short.
are you free after work tomorrow?
add that i would like to go for a walk, but do not choose for them.
would you like to go for a walk after work tomorrow if you are free?
now they say they are not free. write a kind reply without asking another question.
thank you for telling me, and i hope we can find another time.
leave out hope, but keep it one sentence.
thank you for telling me, and we can find another time.
i do not want to choose another time yet either. just thank them.
thank you for telling me.
why did the last reply leave the plan open?
it gave thanks without saying when you would meet or asking your friend to choose. you asked me to keep only the thank you.
now give the thank you alone again.
thank you for telling me.
